instructions: Speak confidently and conversationally, like a senior product manager giving a live technical demo to an engineering audience. Clear enunciation, steady medium pace, warm but precise. Light inflection on key terms. No hype, no salesiness, no pauses between sentences. Flow naturally from one thought to the next.

scenes.title: Ask BC — inside the BigCommerce control panel
scenes.caption: This is Ask BC running live inside the BigCommerce admin. It's a real marketplace app — one-click install, embedded in the iframe, authenticated via OAuth. The green dot means the browser is connected directly to a Cloudflare Worker via WebSocket. Six suggestion chips. A text input. That's the whole surface.

scenes.title: One question, six metrics
scenes.caption: The merchant asks for a store summary. The agent writes one TypeScript script that calls four APIs in parallel — products, customers, orders, channels — and returns six KPI cards. One hundred nineteen products, one hundred twenty-seven customers, forty-seven orders, four sales channels. The tool indicator says 'Used one tool' because all four API calls happened inside a single Codemode execution.

scenes.title: Structured tables with follow-up suggestions
scenes.caption: Five most expensive products as a DataTable. Product name, price right-aligned, SKU, stock level. The agent notes two premium items are out of stock. Below the response: copy button, thumbs up and down for feedback, and two follow-up suggestion chips generated from the response content. One click to drill deeper.

scenes.title: Three-way join — orders, line items, customers
scenes.caption: Five completed orders with per-line-item breakdowns. Products, orders, and line items joined in memory from three different API surfaces in a single script execution. Unit prices, quantities, line totals, order totals. The summary computes the combined revenue across all five orders: seven thousand seven hundred ninety-eight dollars.

scenes.title: Transparent tool usage
scenes.caption: Every response shows which tools the agent called. Click to expand and see the exact API surfaces. Not a black box — the merchant can see that the agent called 'code execution' which internally queried orders and order products. Every query is traceable.

scenes.title: Write operations — preview before execution
scenes.caption: The merchant says 'create a coupon called REEL twenty-five for twenty-five percent off.' The agent calls createCoupon with confirmed false — a preview. The WriteApproval card shows the arguments: name, code, type percentage discount, amount twenty-five, enabled. The agent asks the merchant to confirm before creating.

scenes.title: Confirmed and created — verified in BigCommerce
scenes.caption: The merchant says 'yes, create it.' The agent calls createCoupon again with confirmed true. BigCommerce returns coupon ID four. The confirmation card shows EXECUTED with a green strip. Code REEL twenty-five, twenty-five percent off, active, no expiration. Two-turn confirmation — the store only changed because the merchant explicitly said yes.

scenes.title: How-to questions with step-by-step guidance
scenes.caption: The merchant asks 'how do I set up free shipping on orders over fifty dollars.' The agent doesn't just search docs — it gives three options: create a coupon, configure shipping methods in the admin, or set up an automatic promotion. Each with specific navigation paths. And then offers to create the coupon right there in the chat.

scenes.title: Why Codemode — the model writes TypeScript
scenes.caption: Under the hood, the model writes TypeScript that runs in a Dynamic Worker sandbox with zero network access. The only way out is codemode-dot-star RPC calls that resolve to typed tool functions in the host worker. The host holds the BigCommerce access token. The sandbox never sees it. Promise-dot-all for parallelism. In-memory joins. Guest checkout filtering. One script replaces ten serial tool calls.

scenes.title: Hybrid architecture — Vercel for the UI, Cloudflare for the agent
scenes.caption: Next.js on Vercel handles OAuth, the iframe shell, and the chat UI with generative block components. The Cloudflare Worker handles the agent runtime — Project Think as the base class, Codemode for execution, a Durable Object per store for session persistence, and Dynamic Workers for sandboxed code execution. The browser connects directly to the Worker via WebSocket. Credentials are encrypted in Upstash Redis and resolved per store at runtime.

scenes.title: Twenty-nine curated tools from BigCommerce's OpenAPI specs
scenes.caption: Fourteen OpenAPI specs pulled from BigCommerce's public docs, run through openapi-typescript to generate forty-one thousand lines of typed definitions. Twenty-two read tools inside the Codemode sandbox covering products, orders, customers, inventory, shipping, tax, channels, and help docs. Seven write tools outside the sandbox with two-turn confirmation — coupons, inventory, visibility, pricing, order status, and product creation. All backed by openapi-fetch with typed path validation.

scenes.title: Your store, operating itself
scenes.caption: That's Ask BC. A real marketplace app in the BigCommerce control panel. Generative UI components that render platform-native. Write operations that mutate store state with merchant confirmation. Twenty-nine curated tools powered by Codemode. The merchant doesn't learn a new tool. They just tell the store what they want, and the store does it.
